# Implement block: Switcher Deck Nav (React Native)

You are adding the "Switcher Deck Nav" block from Native Cook to the user's React Native app. The block already exists as working code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

A four-page photo journal, "Slow Departures": a cream feed with a dusk station photo and two smaller platform shots, a dark entry page under an airplane-window photo with altitude, local time and flight length, a pale blue-grey route map drawn with a rail line, a dashed flight arc and five stops above a "Next stop" card, and a navy profile with stats and a grid of saved frames. Every page ends in a small handle, a plain pill above the bottom edge. Pulling the handle up shrinks the page under the finger into a card while the other pages slide in beside it, fanned over a dark warm backdrop as an app-switcher deck in perspective: pages to the right lie on top and spread wide, pages to the left tuck under, recede and darken, each with a glass title chip over its top-left corner, under "Slow Departures" and a count of open pages. The deck scrolls sideways with momentum; tapping a page zooms it back to the full screen, flicking one up closes it while the rest close the gap, and a "Reopen closed pages" chip brings them back.

**Motion.** In the deck a page is 0.6 of the screen, centred 22 pt below the middle. A page p places from the front (its slot minus the deck's scroll) sits 0.6·W·p·(0.56 + 0.15·tanh p) from the centre, so pages to the right spread wider than pages to the left; pages to the left also shrink 4.5% per place (up to three) and darken 20% per place up to 55%. Every page is turned about its upright axis, right edge away, through a 1100 pt perspective: 30° three places left, 17° in front, 8° three places right, interpolated between. Corner radius goes from 0 at the full screen to 50 pt once the page has shrunk 8% and 38 pt (about 23 pt on screen) in the deck; the title chips fade in and rise 30 pt over the last 45% of the opening. Pulling the handle (the bottom 70 pt) opens the deck by the finger's travel over 42% of the screen height, rubber-banded past fully open, and the page follows the finger sideways at 55%; the other pages wait 1.15 screen widths off to their side and slide in as it opens, fading in 1.6 times as fast. A release is projected 0.18 s ahead: past 0.38 the deck opens on a spring (560 ms, damping ratio 0.82) that carries the finger's speed, with a light haptic; otherwise the page falls back (420 ms, 0.8). Dragging sideways scrolls one page per 33% of the screen width, rubber-banded at the ends; a release is thrown 0.22 s ahead and snaps to a page on a spring (620 ms, 0.88) with the finger's speed, with a selection haptic each time a page reaches the front under the finger. Tapping a page (or the backdrop, for the front page) zooms it back to the full screen on a spring (540 ms, 0.9) while the pages to its right slide away, with a light haptic. Flicking a page up lifts it with the finger and fades it over half the screen's height; faster than 800 pt/s or past 28% of its height it flies off 0.8 screens in 300 ms on a strong ease-out (0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) with a medium haptic, and the pages after it slide one slot left on a spring (520 ms, 0.84); the last page cannot be closed and only gives 40 pt. Reopened pages fade in over 420 ms at their slots, growing from 92%. The self-playing demo loops every 12 s from the journal at full screen: a virtual finger (a translucent circle) lands on the handle pill (54 × 5 pt, 12 pt above the bottom safe area) and pulls it half open over 0.8 s from 0.9 s and lets go into the opening spring; flicks across the deck at 2.75 s, 3.95 s and 5.0 s (the deck follows the finger for 0.7 of a page per page, then is thrown) go to the route map, the profile and back to the map; a tap at 6.25 s opens the map; the handle is pulled again at 7.55 s, the deck flicked back to the journal at 9.25 s, and a tap at 10.45 s opens the journal, which rests until the loop starts over. A touch stops the demo for 5 s; it then reopens closed pages and brings the journal back through the deck over 2.2 s before starting over. Under reduced motion the demo does not play and every spring becomes a 220 ms ease-out with no overshoot; the deck still follows the finger.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

### Demo (start here)

- [index.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/navigation/switcher-deck-nav/index.tsx)

### Files of the block

- [SwitcherDeckNav.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/navigation/switcher-deck-nav/SwitcherDeckNav.tsx)
- [SwitcherDeckScreens.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/navigation/switcher-deck-nav/SwitcherDeckScreens.tsx)

### Packages

- `expo-haptics`
- `expo-image`
- `expo-linear-gradient`
- `expo-status-bar`
- `react-native-gesture-handler`
- `react-native-reanimated`
- `react-native-safe-area-context`
- `react-native-svg`
- `react-native-worklets`

The versions the block was built with are in [react-native/package.json](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/package.json).

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced React Native engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on iOS or Android: a simulator, an emulator or a device. A browser is never proof. Do not open the app on the web to check it, not even when the mobile build fails.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is a React Native app, Expo or bare. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- Expo (managed or prebuild) or bare React Native, and the versions of React Native and the Expo SDK.
- The package manager, and how the app is started: Expo Go, a development build, or `react-native run-ios` / `run-android`.
- Navigation: Expo Router, React Navigation, something else, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- Conventions: TypeScript or not, path aliases, how styles are written, where components and screens live.
- Which of the block's packages are already installed, and at which versions.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file it imports. The list above names every file of the block, so you do not have to guess.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo renders, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's props and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's packages with the host's. Install what is missing with the project's own tool (`npx expo install …` in an Expo app, so versions match its SDK).
- A package with native code needs a new native build, and Expo Go only runs the modules it ships with. Say so before you install one, and say which build the user will need.
- If the host is on older versions and an API differs, adapt the block's code to the host. Do not upgrade the host's React Native, Expo SDK or animation libraries without asking.
- Put the files where this app keeps its components. Ask only when two places are equally reasonable and the choice matters.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files, keep their names, and rewrite imports to this project's paths and aliases.
- Copy its images and fonts with it, and load fonts the way the project already does.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility labels as they are in the source.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or route named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Typecheck and lint with the project's own commands and fix what the block introduced.
- Run the app on the user's usual mobile target and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with reduced motion on.
- If the simulator, the emulator or the native build fails, report the error and ask how to continue. Do not fall back to the web.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, packages installed, and whether a new native build is needed.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
